title: The battle-of-the-bands tour with Kirk, Moten and Chick Webb
summary: He describes a tour of up to seven bands playing one-nighters in battle format, with Moten breaking it up with Moten Swing.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: After that, I came back here again, and there was a five-band tour of Andy Kirk, Bennie Moten (it was Count Basie, you know, but it was Bennie's band then), Chick Webb... That's three of them. Zack Whyte, that's four. And... First it was more than that many bands. I think we
had around seven bands to start off with. We had Vernon Andrade. We had Johnson's Happy Pals(X) out of Richmond, Virginia. And I'm trying to think of the other bands. There was Andy Kirk...

Bennie Moten. Andy Kirk and Bennie Moten. Zach Whyte. Chick Webb. And there was a fifth band, I'm trying to think... Maybe it was Johnson's Happy Pals(X), I suppose. But there were supposed to have been seven bands on that tour. I'm trying to think of what that other band was.
What kind of a tour was it, that it was so many bands?

You remember when they used to have battles of the bands; you know, this band battling the other band? That's what it was. And then they all played at the same place in one night; you know, one-nighters. They had some big crowds coming. And...
Would people come to those things as much to listen as to dance?
Yes. Oh yeah. And Bennie Moten used to break it up with the 'Moten Swing.' He capped everybody with that. That would do it, you know!
